originalTitle: Sebi eases rules on use of depository investor protection fund income
simplifiedContent: Sebi, which is like a referee for the stock market, has made a rule change. They now allow companies that hold and manage stocks (called depositories) to use a small part of the money they get from a special fund called the Investor Protection Fund. This money can be used for things like paying bills and meeting legal requirements. Most of the money in the fund will still be kept safe, and this new rule starts in September. This change might help depositories manage their costs, which could be good for the overall functioning of the stock market.

originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Wednesday
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market went down after four days of going up, because some investors sold their stocks to make a profit and there were negative signs from other countries. This made investors a bit nervous, especially since they're waiting to see what the US Federal Reserve (or "US Fed") says in their upcoming report. Despite this, technology stocks (or "IT stocks") did relatively well. Analysts think that the stock market's direction in the short term will depend on how well companies are doing, how the monsoon season is progressing, the stability of the Indian rupee, and whether foreign investors are putting money into the market. These factors will likely influence what happens in the market on Wednesday.

originalTitle: SanDisk shares crash 10% as AI chip selloff spreads to memory stocks
simplifiedContent: SanDisk's stock price fell by 10% due to a sell-off of stocks related to artificial intelligence (AI) chips, which also affected other memory-related stocks. This means that investors are selling their shares in companies that make memory chips, like SanDisk, Micron, and Intel. The sell-off is a continuation of a trend where stocks related to AI and tech are falling after a previous rally. This matters because it can impact the overall value of investments in these companies and the tech industry as a whole. The fall in stock prices may be a sign that the AI-related stock rally is coming to an end, at least for now.

originalTitle: Kusumgar raises  ₹194 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO opening tomorrow
simplifiedContent: Kusumgar Limited, a company that's about to sell its shares to the public, has already raised ₹193.9 crore from a group of big investors. These investors, called anchor investors, bought 4,628,877 shares at a price of ₹419 each. This happened before the company's Initial Public Offering (IPO) opens to everyone else tomorrow, on July 8, 2026. The company is selling a total of 1.55 crore shares, which is expected to bring in ₹650 crore. This is important because it shows that big investors are interested in buying the company's shares, which might attract individual investors to buy in as well.

originalTitle: Gold, silver prices today: Comex gold and silver edge lower amid Middle East tensions, firm US dollar
simplifiedContent: The prices of gold and silver went down on July 7th. This happened because of rising tensions in the Middle East and a stronger US dollar. The value of these precious metals is often affected by what's happening in the world and by changes in the dollar's value. As a result, gold and silver futures, which are like bets on what their prices will be in the future, also dropped. This is important because it shows how global events can impact the prices of these investments.

originalTitle: Bust or boom ahead? Here's why Warren Buffett successor's $10 billion bet on big tech has divided experts
simplifiedContent: Greg Abel, the person who will take over Warren Buffett's company Berkshire Hathaway, has invested $10 billion in big tech companies, which has caused some experts to disagree. This investment is notable because Berkshire Hathaway has a lot of extra money, $400 billion, that it can use to invest. Some experts are skeptical about this investment strategy, especially since it involves buying stock in companies like Alphabet, which is a big tech company. This matters because it could affect the performance of Berkshire Hathaway and the value of its investments. The skepticism is partly due to concerns about the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on these tech companies.
